text.text_excerpt: Let the gluttony begin!!! This is one of my favorite events of the year. The $99 entry fee keeps some people away, and I'm not sure I want them to know what they are missing. It's for charity y'all!!! This year it filled up every inch of Champion Square, and extended to the front doors of the Superdome. The stage hosted several crowed pleasing acts (no big names, only big sound). 50 chefs prepared their take on boudin. This included traditional Cajun boudin, blood boudin, soups, dumplings, pâté, blood velvet cupcakes with lard icing and everything in between. We made it through 1 tent and the headliners and couldn't try another bite! I was sad, but oh so happy all at the same time. Buffal...

Very fun event that is well worth the ticket price and for a good cause. The food is plentiful and delicious and comes courtesy of many of the city and region's top restaurants. The cocktails are available everywhere you turn and are deliciously crafted. Considering the amount of attendees, the food lines were very manageable. The only excessive wait we encountered was the popular neat bourbon pour line. One bartender? Bad idea. Music was fun and raucous, though Elle King was likely more entertaining via her intoxication and dirty mouth, rather than her music. Cheers, Emeril! A lovely event you've got here.

When David told me that our favorite band, Nathaniel Rateliff and The Night Sweats, was coming to NOLA for the second time this year and playing Emeril Lagasse's Boudin, Bourbon and Beer fundraiser, I knew that we somehow had to get in. We've seen this band two other times and they always put on a fantastic show. I had no idea that unlimited food and alcohol was also a part of the party. After a little luck, we were able to secure some passes and we were ready for action. First of all, the food at this event is incredible.
